purpose: Zero-oracle execution gate for the PMO scored pilot. Each run drove the real execute_task path with an injected free scorer; no oracle was ever constructed or called.

free_smoke.note: First gate, on the pre-Defect-1 bytes. Stopped with pkill before writing result files; its evidence is the round counts below, which established that the bootstrap-pool continuity fix and the gsk3b_asset contract fix both hold far past the round-6 failure that killed the previous scored attempt.

free_smoke_250.note: First gate at the contract budget.

free_smoke_final.note: Re-run after the budget threading and AUC denominator fix.

free_smoke_launch.note: Final gate on the exact sealed bytes the scored run launched from.

free_smoke_oracle_fix.note: Re-run on the corrected worker and the re-sealed contract chain, after the gsk3b oracle asset-resolution fix. The chain refused the first attempt with an input identity mismatch on the edited worker, which is the guard working.

gate_criteria: free_evaluations == budget (the authorized budget is fully exercised)
at least one bootstrap pool recorded
archive grows beyond INIT_COUNT, i.e. children re-enter as parents
known_limitation: This gate calls execute_task directly with an injected free scorer, so it never exercises the Modal worker's post-processing AND never constructs or calls a TDC oracle. It therefore cannot see either of the two defects that reached a scored launch: a result-key rename, covered statically by tests/test_pmo_worker_result_contract.py, and an oracle whose asset never resolves, covered by the in-image positive control in diagnostics/pmo_oracle_asset_audit_v1.json and enforced by the worker before it charges a call.
